findings.reason: Confirmed, and I would have fixed it: the audit's sentence is a false mathematical statement about a declaration it cites. I read Mathlib's definition rather than its name. IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup is `Subgroup (K / n)` with carrier {x : K/n | for all v not in S, v.valuationOfNeZeroMod n x = 1}, where the file's local notation sets K / n to be Kˣ ⧸ (powMonoidHom n).range, i.e. Kˣ modulo nth powers. So K(S,n) is the group of field power classes whose valuation is divisible by n outside S, defined by a valuation condition and not by having an S-unit representative — exactly as the finding says, and not 'the group K(S,n) of S-units mod n-th powers'. Mathlib's own file makes the containment visible in the other direction: fromUnit is a homomorphism Rˣ →* K(∅,n) and fromUnit_ker shows its kernel is the nth powers of Rˣ, so unit power classes inject into the Selmer group as a subgroup. The quotient is the class-group torsion the audit drops, and Tau Ceti proves it: the module docstring of TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger/SelmerGroup/Basic.lean labels fromSUnitLift_injective 'exactness on the left', ker_toClassGroup 'exactness in the middle' and range_toClassGroup 'exactness on the right', and I read the statements — ker_toClassGroup proves (toClassGroup K S n).ker = (fromSUnit K S n).range, and range_toClassGroup, under [NeZero n], proves (toClassGroup K S n).range = (powMonoidHom n : ClassGroup (S.integer K) →* ClassGroup (S.integer K)).ker. That is the sequence 1 → O_S^×/(O_S^×)^n → K(S,n) → Cl(O_S)[n] → 1 the finding states, so an identification with S-unit power classes holds only when Cl(O_S)[n] is trivial. The finding's second point is also right, and I checked it separately: the audit calls selmerGroup 'the target of the S-restricted Kummer map' in a note whose other cited declaration is TauCeti.kummerClassMap, and that map's type is into Multiplicative (H1 (AbsoluteGaloisGroup K) (KummerCoeff K n)) — its target is H¹, not the Selmer group, so the sentence does obscure the direction. The proposed fix is the right one: state the valuation-divisibility definition, record the proved exact sequence with its three declarations, and distinguish the map of power classes into H¹ from the algebraic S-unit map into K(S,n). Two qualifications a fix job should carry. First, nothing here changes the layer: the target stays `library: partial` and the layer stays `partly built`, since the rest of the note — the finite-level Kummer injection and kernel, and the absence of the p-adic limit, the Z_p(1) coefficient module and the tensor-product comparison — is accurate and independently supported, so the correction is confined to the final sentence. Second, `high` is defensible but rests on the consequence rather than the scope: the error would lead a worker to consume selmerGroup as O_S^×/(O_S^×)^n and prove a false statement, even though the declaration is cited only as `related`. Verification tree: I read Mathlib at 045acef0f761280401116e3801cb78ed1b2e716b and Tau Ceti at 787733ab7904b5650f41f0f62e3da361dd27b254, not the pinned 082e2d3 and f790474. Every declaration the finding names was present with the stated content, and fromSUnitLift sits at the cited line 154; small line drift from the pins is possible and none of the statements or hypotheses differed from what the finding reports.

Confirmed, and I would have fixed it. The audit's L3 note says Mathlib has 'abstract measures on Z_p with values in Q_p and the Amice transform identifying them with power series', and cites AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv. I read the file. The equivalence is `def amiceTransformEquiv : D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]] ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧` — measures with values in ℤ_[p], identified with ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧, so the coefficient domain in the note is wrong. The generic version at `def amiceTransform : D(ℤ_[p], R) →ₗ[R] R⟦X⟧` does allow general coefficients but is only a linear map, not an equivalence, exactly as the finding says; the file's own module docstring draws the same distinction, describing amiceTransform as 'the Amice transform as an `R`-linear map into `R⟦X⟧`' and amiceTransformEquiv as 'the Amice transform with `ℤ_[p]`-coefficients, bundled' as a linear equivalence, and the line above the definition points from the map to the equivalence. So a reader of the audit would believe Mathlib supplies a ℚ_p-coefficient identification that it does not. The proposed fix is right and complete: replace ℚ_p by ℤ_[p], give the actual linear-equivalence type, and cite only the generic transform if ℚ_p-valued measures are mentioned at all. I agree with the finding that the layer verdict must not move — the target stays absent, because the cited equivalence supplies neither the completed-group-ring identification nor control theory, characteristic ideals or Γ-module theory, and the note's own observation that this is an analytic object rather than Z_p[[Γ]] is untouched by the correction. Severity `medium` is right: the claim is false as written and misdescribes the library baseline, but the verdict and the missing-work conclusion are unaffected. Verification tree: Mathlib at 045acef0f761280401116e3801cb78ed1b2e716b rather than the pinned 082e2d3; amiceTransformEquiv is at line 157 in that tree against the cited 156, a one-line drift with identical content.
